g.text: More expressive models do not calibrate better

g.title: common expectation adopting more advanced expressive architectures inherently improve calibration
g.desc: There is a common expectation that adopting more advanced or expressive architectures will inherently improve calibration.

g.title: through controlled case study structural distortion benchmark demonstrate expectation false graph transformers positional encodings do not improve calibration vanilla message-passing increasing model size worse
g.desc: Through a controlled case study on a structural distortion benchmark, the authors demonstrate this expectation is false: graph transformers and positional encodings do not meaningfully improve calibration over vanilla message-passing networks, and increasing model size can even make calibration worse.
g.text: As rotation grows, accuracy drops as expected — but expected calibration error grows sharply too. Transformers (GPS),
deeper and wider models do not fix it; only G-ΔUQ cuts ECE while keeping accuracy close to the vanilla model.

g.title: finding motivates different path
g.desc: This finding motivates a different path.

g.title: rather chasing expressivity paper advocates epistemic uncertainty quantification directly modulate confidence indicators
g.desc: Rather than chasing expressivity, the paper advocates for epistemic uncertainty quantification to directly modulate confidence indicators.
g.text: Instead of chasing more expressive architectures, use epistemic uncertainty
quantification to directly modulate the confidence indicators the model reports —
so calibration improves without redesigning the backbone.
